column1: # The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (Donkey Kong Bananza's figure). The NPDM declares 48 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on.

# nninitStartup asks SetHeapSize 0x18ce00000 (6.2 GB) with the 9 GB pool, as Mario Kart World. 256 MB in front + 4 GB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 8 GB heap region: a starting split, to be measured
# kid-with-sword-remake L6.1: an 8 GB alias region on the iPhone (the Mac takes 64 GB whatever the profile says, hle_svc.c). With 4 GB, play filled it to 3.75 GB (logs 40,
# 42, 44: "alias region mapped up to +3.75 GB"), and the cutscene after the Master Sword stopped on its first picture, a white screen, on iPhones only (nxnative issue #2407);
# the Mac, with its 64 GB, plays it. The block grows by the same 4 GB: 256 MB + 8 GB alias + 256 MB stack + 8 GB heap. It is address space: the 9 GB pool still bounds what is mapped
# kid-with-sword-remake L6.1: no application-pool check on the guest's maps. At the Master Sword (an iPhone log of the white screen, L-series before L3): the game holds its
# 6.2 GB heap, asks MapPhysicalMemory for 38 MB more as the cutscene starts, and is refused ("2.73 GB mapped, the application pool is full"); the SDK frees cached pages and
# retries, the cutscene's AV1 decoder never opens, and the fade-in stays white for good. Without the check the map is made (with the 8 GB alias region above to hold it); the
# guest's memory is in files on the iPhone (DM_GUEST_FILE), so pages it maps and does not touch cost nothing
# The game steps its time by a frame ratio, its base rate / its frame rate, whatever the frame took: frames longer than a vsync played in slow motion. The ratio takes the host's
# frame step instead (MATCH_FRAME_STEP in patches.py, found by its function on any build that keeps it): 1 vsync at 60 fps, 2 when 60 does not hold, so game time = real time

# As Tears of the Kingdom: the terrain's height, blend and hole maps are written by the CPU into textures after they are created. Without these keys they stay zero: holes in the ground and the wrong materials
# The fork's steady 30 fps (V17): at 30 fps an iPhone lowers the GPU clock until the work fills most of the frame (log 60: 195 of 300 frames over 33.3 ms, 109 payback steps in 40 s).
# the display link's frame latency 2 at the 30 fps cap: 66 ms from submission to display instead of 33, so a 34-38 ms frame is absorbed while the mean fits
# no payback: a late frame's lost time is let go (the game slows by it, as on the console) instead of a step of 3 vsyncs shown for 2, a half-frame jump in motion on the next frame
# The touch controls' Forest colours: blue A, green B, yellow X / Y, red +, deep green shoulders, bronze D-pad, gold rims, all translucent (DmGamepad.m theme_init)
# FF (the kid-with-sword-remake fork's experimental iPhone build of nxnative main): the iPhone's settings from the fork's X line.
# Render pipelines through Metal 4 with hybrid stand-ins, the pipeline bases built on the phone (L2): one IPA for every iPhone, no archive made offline. Build it with --gpu none
# (the NSP script; pso_gpu has no "none", and without it the profile would get the A19's archive). The first start builds the base of every shader pair behind "Preparing pipelines"
# (pso_prebuild, about 37,000), once per chain version and iOS major version, into the app's pso_archive/; later starts take them from there.
# Why not the MTLDevice path without bases (FF12 and L1, as the fork's Mario Kart World port): every pipeline the prewarm lists did not hold was built while the frame waited, and this
# game has about 37,000 shader pairs against the lists' 4,443 render pipelines. An iPhone 18 Pro (log 30, L1, 30 fps) built 264 such pipelines at about 213 ms each in 212 s of play:
# 56 s of freezes, the worst 8-10 s for 30-37 pipelines at once. With bases a draw takes its stand-in at once and its own pipeline comes from the background.
# Before (X3 to FF11): pso_mtl4 on and pso_gpu g19p, the iPhone 18 Pro's archive made offline and shipped in the app (4.9 GB)
# Frame buffering: each present is copied, so the game's swapchain texture is free at once (the fork's V17, a steady 30 fps)
# Handheld, as an iPhone runs it: the game presents 1920x1080 instead of 2048x1152 docked
# Pool tables give a finalized texture's ID the dummy instead of making its texture again: about 2.5 GB at the house-to-forest change (upstream PR #1393, open)

# The Render scale slider (the fork's V15-touch2): a fixed fraction of the game's base size, from 0.25 (480x270 handheld, marked Potato) to 1.0 (1920x1080); the render-scale stub (patches.py) fixes every value up to 1.0

# The game upscales through a chain: agl_ndsr_vr feature pass, network and blend at the render size, agl_ndsr_vr_light scale to 1920x1080. DM_UPSCALER=metalfx skips the chain for MetalFX (nvn_mtl.m up_chain)
# dispatch_overlap went with the merge of nxnative main (L3): the host now orders every game's dispatches by the game's own barriers (nvn_mtl.m dispatch_enc_cs,
# DM_NVN_DISPATCH_BARRIER), which covers what the key did here (117 dispatches at the start of a Kokiri Forest frame, 5.7 -> 3.7 ms on an M4 Pro)
# amiibo: the game's Game/AmiiboSetting file in three variants (scripts/oot_amiibo_overlay.py into the romfs_overlay folder): the daily limit off, the drop chances doubled, or both
# The 3D views' size at render scale 1.0, docked then handheld, for the launcher's Render scale row in pixels (settings.py render_base): the game renders its 3D at 65/64 of the
# output's height times the scale (a Mac run and the owner's iPhone logs at 0.6: handheld 1169x658 for 1920x1080, Wide view's 1432x658 for 2352x1080, docked 1909x877 for 3136x1440)
# and its width from that height and the output's shape (LauncherSettings.swift rangeLabel takes Wide view's shape from the screen)
# kid-with-sword-remake L8: with a mod on, the game reads no input for the first 660 presented frames (about 20-25 s from start; a "Getting ready" banner on iPhone). A mod's
# piece of Link set up before about frame 600 is never drawn that session (the Goku mod, 23 launches: every setup at frame 589 or earlier invisible, at 680 or later drawn; the
# game's reason not found), and a save cannot be loaded before the hold ends, so the setup lands after it. Without mods there is no hold. DM_MOD_INPUT_HOLD=<frames> overrides
